note: Mauritius's largest banks are MCB, SBM and Absa Bank (Mauritius); MCB's and Absa's price lists were read, and SBM's wasn't reached. MCB's statement of interest rates and service charges (last updated 7 October 2026), read for every personal credit card: the rate is the prime lending rate of 6.90% plus a margin, 9.50% on the American Express Green and Gold and the VISA Platinum and Signature (16.40% a year) and 13.50% on the MasterCard/VISA Classic and Gold and the MasterCard PRIMO (20.40%); primary cards cost 1,500, 3,000, 1,500, 2,500, 200, 950 and 150 rupees a year before VAT, whose rate the list doesn't state (so it isn't written); a cash advance costs a flat 100 rupees locally (2% abroad, not written); going over the limit costs 200 rupees on the first four and 150 on the rest; conversion is 2.50%. The card the file named before, 'MasterCard/ VISA Classic', is kept with its terms extended; the 'MasterCard/ VISA' cards are written as one card each, as the list prices them. Absa Bank (Mauritius)'s personal tariff guide (effective 1 June 2026): its Platinum, Gold and Classic credit cards cost 1,725, 1,092.50 and 230 rupees a year with VAT, no joining fee, 2.13% a month, 2.10% for a cash advance (at least 150 rupees), 3% forex, 400 rupees for a returned payment, a minimum payment of 5% (at least 2,000, 1,000 and 100 rupees) and up to 52 days interest free; its late and excess-limit fees, each '1% of amount due' (at least 250 and 200 rupees), don't make clear whether the amount due is the minimum or the balance, so they aren't written. Business, corporate and foreign-currency cards aren't written.
